Item: How wide should the bed be?
Prompt / specification: A generous planting area fails when the center requires stepping into and compacting the soil. Options: Set width from tested reach on every accessible side | Use a wider bed with a deliberate central access path | Use four feet wide against a wall

Side force increases with soil depth, water, span, and loss of connection stiffness over time. Options: Use corners and intermediate braces sized for the declared height and span | Reduce bed height or side-bay length | Add soil first and brace if the boards bow

A blanket liner can block drainage, trap roots, or create a perched water layer. Options: Keep an open draining base and use only purpose-specific permeable barriers | Use a raised contained floor only for a designed accessible planter | Install an impermeable sheet without an engineered outlet

Prompt / specification: Divide the bed into reachable, braced, draining bays with accessible irrigation and paths.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Bed plan with structural bays, paths, and fill sequence. Hold: Stop if soil delivery would arrive before the empty structure can be inspected.

Prompt / specification: Prepare durable side, corner, brace, and cap parts with protected ends and repeatable bay lengths.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Labeled parts and approved connection/material sample. Hold: Stop on unsuitable treated material, split ends, weak edge distance, or incompatible metal.

Prompt / specification: Build a square empty bed and prove every brace and irrigation route before soil conceals it.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Square empty bed with complete structural and drainage inspection. Hold: Stop if sides move under hand pressure or drainage fabric bridges outlets.

Prompt / specification: Place, level, and stabilize the bed while preserving site drainage and path geometry.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Final site, path, level, and drainage record before fill. Hold: Stop if leveling sends runoff toward a structure or path width is lost.

Prompt / specification: Fill in controlled lifts, observe side movement and drainage, and retain maintenance access.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Filled-bed inspection with before/after side measurements. Hold: Do not close after bowing, joint movement, standing water, or path settlement.

Prompt / specification: Use when paths remain available along both long sides and the tested reach meets at the center without stepping in soil.
Project value / evidence: A wider productive zone is possible, while irrigation, trellis orientation, and mid-span braces must remain reachable from either side.

Prompt / specification: Use only when a narrower tested reach serves the rear crop row and the fence retains required inspection access.
Project value / evidence: Width decreases and rear fasteners, weeds, irrigation, and trellis work need a planned front-access sequence.

Prompt / specification: Use when a qualified structural design provides a supported floor, drainage, and approach clearance above ground.
Project value / evidence: It is no longer a simple open-bottom bed; saturated-floor load, outlet maintenance, and accessibility geometry govern the build.

Prompt / specification: Planting, weeding, or harvest requires stepping in soil or leaning beyond the approved reach mockup.
Project value / evidence: Reduce bed width or add a deliberate non-soil access path before filling and planting the affected bay.

Prompt / specification: Side boards move outward, brace gaps open, or corner fasteners rotate during staged fill or watering.
Project value / evidence: Stop filling, unload the affected lift safely, and add or redesign corner and intermediate restraint before resuming.

Prompt / specification: Water stands above an impermeable layer or drains only through an unverified puncture after irrigation.
Project value / evidence: Remove fill as needed, restore a purposeful permeable or engineered outlet path, and retest empty before refill.

Prompt / specification: Bulk delivery blocks paths or pressures the team to fill before square, brace, utility, and drainage checks pass.
Project value / evidence: Hold or relocate delivery and complete the empty-bed inspection; schedule pressure cannot substitute for structural evidence.

Prompt / specification: The raised bed remains a reachable, draining garden after saturated soil is added, with observable structure and repair access around every loaded bay.
Every planting point can be reached from the approved path without stepping into soil or loading the side wall.
Before-and-after measurements show no continuing side bow, corner opening, brace movement, or path settlement after watering.
A full irrigation test drains through the intended ground or engineered outlet without standing water against side members.
Paths, irrigation valves, trellis connections, braces, and replaceable side fasteners remain accessible after final fill.
